description: Runs a command in the Mac owner's login shell (zsh), as them, never as administrator. Waits up to wait seconds (default and most 30); a longer command keeps running as a job (check it with shell_check). With job and input: types input into that job (then Enter unless enter is false). With job and stop: stops it (Ctrl-C, then forcibly). A command writes only to its own scratch folder ($LATCHKEY_SCRATCH, also $TMPDIR; moved to the Trash when it finishes), the folder it runs in (unless that is the home folder), Downloads, and package caches; anything else fails unless declared in writes (with why), and so does changing settings (defaults write: declare ~/Library/Preferences/<domain>.plist). Opening apps, files, or links through macOS (open) fails unless declared in uses, and opens them behind the app the owner is using (/usr/bin/open brings it to the front, when the owner wants to see it); a program with windows (an app such as Chrome or Preview, even headless) also starts only with open declared (Chrome needs --no-sandbox too), and /usr/bin/log never runs inside the fence; builds work (xcodebuild and swift, also from make and scripts, run with their own sandboxes turned off, since macOS can't start one inside the fence; give xcodebuild a -derivedDataPath it may write, and declare open to build a Swift package folder with xcodebuild, which swift build doesn't need, or an app whose icon was made in Icon Composer); scripting other apps (osascript) and starting background services (launchctl, brew services) aren't possible. Whatever it leaves running is stopped when it finishes, unless keep_minutes asks to keep it (checking the job keeps it longer; 24 hours at most).

enter.description: With input: press Enter after (default true)

job.description: A running job's id, to type into or stop

keep_minutes.description: Keep what the command leaves running (a server, a watcher) and its scratch folder this many minutes after it finishes (0 to 1440, default 0)

machine.description: The machine to use, by name, as the machines tool lists it. Leave it out when only one machine offers this tool.

uses.description: What the command does beyond the fence, only when the owner's task needs it: open (apps, files, links through macOS). What it starts runs outside the fence and keeps running.

wait.description: Seconds to wait for it to finish (1 to 30, default 30)

why.description: With writes: what the command writes there, for the owner's list

writes.description: Folders or files outside the allowed places the command will write (full paths or ~/…); results meant to stay

name: shell_run
title: Run a Command
